details: Technical teams from the United States and Iran are engaged in mediated talks in Doha, Qatar, as of June 30 and July 1, 2026. The discussions, aimed at de-escalating tensions over the Strait of Hormuz and implementing a memorandum of understanding, follow recent exchanges of fire. While Iran has ruled out direct meetings with the US, the dialogue focuses on managing the vital shipping lane and the potential release of frozen Iranian assets. Easing tensions typically support risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, by potentially lowering oil prices and reducing geopolitical uncertainty. However, the fragility of the truce suggests continued market caution.
title: US-Iran Dialogue Continues in Doha, Markets Cautiously Optimistic

details: The European Union's Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA) framework became fully enforceable on July 1, 2026, marking the end of its transitional period. This comprehensive regulation requires all crypto-asset service providers in the EU to hold a MiCA license. An estimated 80% of previously registered crypto firms in Europe have not secured this authorization, with major exchanges like Binance facing service restrictions for EU users. The new regulatory landscape aims to bring clarity and consumer protection but is expected to cause short-term disruption, user migration, and a significant consolidation within the European crypto market. Stablecoins like USDT will also face restrictions on regulated platforms.
title: EU MiCA Regulation Takes Full Effect, Reshaping European Crypto Market
